segments.title: Chương 22: 0022 [Vở kịch hay mới chỉ bắt đầu]
segments.content:
Some concepts have long been commonplace, yet breaking through that final layer of understanding is difficult.

The creature known as a "shill" was already everywhere ten years ago.

Shills for restaurants and bars were one thing, but medical shills were universally despised at the time.

No matter which public hospital you went to, inside and out, it was crawling with shills.

Some medical shills would trick patients into going to private hospitals or clinics, where a minor ailment could empty your pockets. Others were actually peddling health supplements, fooling terminally ill patients into not seeing a doctor, claiming their products could cure any disease.

Lotteries were also incredibly popular for a time. Anyone who didn't live through that era could hardly imagine the scene.

When private lotteries were at their most rampant, they even spread to remote rural towns.

Farmers carrying their vegetables to the market in town would encounter a crowd of private lottery operators. They'd arrange for a shill to win the grand prize, and the atmosphere would instantly ignite, with countless farmers pulling out their hard-earned money to try their luck.

Due to their extremely negative impact, private lotteries were strictly banned, but they could never be completely eradicated.

Just last year, when Chen Guiliang was a sophomore in high school, he went to the city to have some fun during the National Day holiday. Along a street just a few hundred meters long, there were over a dozen stalls set up to sell private lottery tickets, and they even hired "Andy Lau" and "Jacky Cheung" impersonators to draw a crowd.

They were just celebrity look-alikes, but they advertised them as the real deal, spreading the word half a month in advance that Andy Lau and Jacky Cheung were coming.

People flocked to see them.

Chen Guiliang had a primary school classmate who started working at a hotpot restaurant right after graduating from junior high. He had painstakingly saved up for two years, only to lose it all in an hour playing the lottery, winning nothing but a lot of laundry detergent, thermoses, and the like.

He got swept up in it. That kind of atmosphere was simply impossible to resist.

Chen Guiliang remembered it very clearly. A shabbily dressed old man from the countryside was invited on stage to be interviewed by the host. The old man just grinned foolishly the whole time, unable to speak clearly, only managing to say that he had casually spent two yuan and won a grand prize of a full 50,000 yuan.

Before the interview was even over, countless onlookers rushed over to buy tickets.

Tao Chenggang naturally knew about what happened during last year's National Day holiday. He even knew two of the private lottery bosses. The rest of them were all bastards who had come up from the south.

Using "Andy Lau" and "Jacky Cheung" for promotion was the brainchild of those southern bosses. The local bosses, in turn, helped smooth things over with the authorities, so they wouldn't get shut down halfway through the lottery.

The thought of running a lottery in his game solidified Tao Chenggang's determination to develop it!

He no longer pressed for more golden ideas. Instead, he said with a smile, "Little brother, how about joining my company? We can start a business and make a game together. You don't need to put in any cash. Just use that game concept as your investment, and I'll convert it into some company shares for you."

"I still have to study. The college entrance exam is next year," Chen Guiliang politely declined.

Tao Chenggang continued his pitch, "It'll take me a good half a year to get everything ready. By the time we officially start making the game, you'll be about to enter university. You can study and run a business at the same time, without either getting in the way. Think about it, you'll be a shareholder in a game company before you even graduate. How cool would you look at school? Even the campus queen will be chasing after you."

These words were incredibly persuasive to a young man.

If Chen Guiliang hadn't been reborn, he probably would have agreed on the spot.

"I need cash. My family is still in debt." Chen Guiliang had his own business ideas and didn't want to be led by others.

In his previous life, his business had been successful, but he'd been through a bitter falling-out with his shareholders. The memory left a bad taste in Chen Guiliang's mouth.

This life, he had to have controlling shares!

Besides, there was no guarantee Tao Chenggang would succeed. There was a high probability he'd lose everything.

When one plan failed, Tao Chenggang brought up his own university days, talking about how all the female students were gold diggers who looked down on the poor.

Chen Guiliang turned a deaf ear, continuing to switch accounts and post inflammatory comments, turning the Mengya Forum into a complete shitshow.

His impervious demeanor left Tao Chenggang speechless.

He was even afraid that if he didn't buy the A4 papers today, Chen Guiliang would turn around and sell them to a big company.

Tao Chenggang finally made another offer: "A flat 50,000 yuan, but it has to be paid in installments. I can give you 10,000 today, and another 10,000 next July. The remaining 30,000 will be paid in a lump sum at the end of next year."

Tao Chenggang's intention was simple: to tie Chen Guiliang down with the final payment, preventing him from selling the idea elsewhere.

He felt that a final payment of 40,000 yuan was enough to keep a high school student in line.

Chen Guiliang, however, was growing more and more surprised. This guy was really willing to put up money to make a game? He really was a bit of a gambler!

Surprised as he was, the negotiation had to continue.

Chen Guiliang shook his head. "50,000 is too little."

"Give me a reasonable price," Tao Chenggang said.

"180,000."

"80,000 yuan, be straight with me!"

After some haggling, Chen Guiliang realized he had misjudged the purchasing power.

Over 100,000 yuan in 2003 was truly a huge sum of money, and it was very difficult to get it with just empty words.

They finally settled on 100,000 yuan, which was a completely unexpected windfall for Chen Guiliang.

Before coming here, he hadn't thought he would succeed at all.

"You have to write an IOU. The down payment must be at least 50,000. The rest can be in installments however you want." Chen Guiliang was already mentally prepared not to receive the final payment.

He only needed this 50,000 yuan as start-up capital. Next, he would set up a private server with Tao Chenggang.

As for the final payment, he didn't care if it was paid or not.

The real show was just beginning.

"No problem," Tao Chenggang agreed without hesitation.

Tao Chenggang called out Yang Yuhui's nickname, "Yangyu, Yangyu, where are your pen, paper, and ink pad?"

Yang Yuhui came in from outside, found the items, and slapped them on the table.

Tao Chenggang quickly wrote out an IOU. He even took out his own ID card, wrote down the ID number, then signed and pressed his thumbprint.

"IOU to Chen Guiliang..."

Yang Yuhui leaned over to look at the IOU. A quick glance left him dumbfounded. He scratched his head in confusion and said, "Brother Gang, I wasn't gone for that long. How come you're giving this kid 100,000 yuan?"

Tao Chenggang laughed. "Little brother said he's going to gift me a fortune. Since he's a man of his word, of course I have to show my appreciation."

"What on earth is going on?" Yang Yuhui's curiosity grew.

"It's a secret," Tao Chenggang closed the ink pad lid and said to Chen Guiliang, "Let's go to the bank now. I'll transfer the first payment to you."

Chen Guiliang reached out and swiped the entire ink pad box, stuffing it into his pocket and saying, "I'll borrow this."

Yang Yuhui followed them all the way to the stairwell, unable to resist tugging on Chen Guiliang's sleeve and asking, "What do you have that's worth 100,000 yuan?"

Chen Guiliang replied with a smile, "Knowledge is wealth. I'm a top student from No. 2 High School."

In the blink of an eye, Tao Chenggang and Chen Guiliang had disappeared.

Yang Yuhui stood there, muttering to himself, "A top student from No. 2 High School is that valuable?"

After a moment of confusion, he took out his phone and called Feng Tao.

"Hey, Feng Lao'er, what's up with your nephew?" Yang Yuhui asked.

Feng Tao was in his shop with his apprentice, installing an operating system for a customer. He asked while working, "Did he get into trouble at Brother Gang's place?"

Yang Yuhui said, "Brother Gang is giving him 100,000 yuan for no reason. 50,000 down, and an IOU for the rest."

"He really sold it for 100,000?" Feng Tao was utterly shocked.

Yang Yuhui asked, "What on earth did he sell to Brother Gang?"

Feng Tao laughed out loud. "That's awesome. He's my nephew, alright."

"Fuck!"

Yang Yuhui was getting anxious. "Hurry up and tell me, you bastard. What did your nephew sell to Brother Gang?"

Feng Tao deliberately kept him in suspense. "You wouldn't understand even if I told you. Hanging up."

"Hey, hey... hey... Fuck!"

After the call, Yang Yuhui grew even more curious. He scratched his head and fidgeted, feeling completely restless.

He went back to the studio to arrange some things, then quickly ran downstairs to catch up with Tao Chenggang.

Red Star Department Store.

Cheng Tao Computer Shop.

A middle-aged woman and her son were sitting beside Feng Tao, watching him install the operating system.

The woman asked, "This isn't Windows 2000, is it? The computers at my workplace use Windows 2000. I heard it's the most advanced system."

Feng Tao loved this kind of customer—plenty of money and no clue about anything. "Ma'am, Windows XP was released in 2001. You can tell which is more advanced just by looking at the release date."

"That makes sense," the woman nodded. "My workplace only has one computer, and we got it two years ago."

Feng Tao said, "Back then, Windows XP hadn't made it to China yet. Ma'am, if your workplace needs new computers, you can get a discount at my shop. I'll even give you a little kickback."

"I'll definitely recommend you," the woman couldn't wait for the kickback and started asking for benefits right away. "I spent several thousand here today, and I'm going to recommend a big client to you, so you should throw in some free gifts."

Feng Tao first hesitated, then gritted his teeth and nodded as if he were taking a huge loss. "Alright, just as a thank you for your business. I can give you the mouse and keyboard for free, and a set of Wubi practice software for your son."

"What a generous boss. You'll definitely get rich," the woman felt like she had gotten a good deal.

Her son, a first-year high school student, sat quietly the entire time, but he was actually incredibly excited, just wanting to take the computer home as soon as possible.

Feng Tao began to brag, "The call I just got was from a friend of mine. Guess what? My nephew sold a proposal for a full 200,000 yuan!"

Exaggerating his accomplishments, falsifying the report.

He had just pulled 100,000 yuan out of thin air.

"What kind of proposal is more expensive than a house?" the woman asked curiously.

Feng Tao said proudly, "A design proposal for an online game."

Although the woman viewed online games as a plague, she was impressed that someone could make money from them. "The boss is so young. How old is your nephew?"

"He's my grand-nephew, my aunt's grandson," Feng Tao said. "He's only 17 this year, and he's a senior in high school."

The woman was surprised. "He made 200,000 yuan as a high school senior? Does he play games a lot?"

Feng Tao smiled. "He's in the experimental class at County No. 2 High School, a top student who can get into any top university. You don't have to be addicted to games to be able to create a game design proposal."

Hearing that he was in the experimental class at County No. 2 High School, the woman was instantly convinced that he was a good student, but she couldn't lose face. "My son goes to City No. 2 High School. The admission score for the high school entrance exam is a few points higher than County No. 2."

The student sitting next to her immediately puffed out his chest upon hearing this.

Feng Tao continued to boast, "My nephew only lost a dozen or so points on his high school entrance exam. If he went to City No. 2, he'd definitely be in the experimental class too. He used to complain to me that he was so stupid for not knowing that someone with a county household registration could also apply to City No. 2 High School. If he had applied to City No. 2 back then, he could have used their acceptance letter to get free tuition at County No. 2."

"That is a shame," the woman nodded.

Feng Tao said, "My nephew is a 'left-behind child.' His parents haven't been home for years. He's had to rely on his own hard work for his studies since he was little."

The woman began to lecture her son, "Yangyang, did you hear that? His parents aren't around, no one is supervising him, and he can still get into the experimental class at County No. 2 High School. You have to work hard from now on. Get good grades when they split into arts and sciences, and try to get selected for the experimental class."

"Mmm," the student responded.

"What 'mmm'? Answer louder when you're spoken to!" the woman said. "Look at him, he's only a high school senior and he's already earned enough for a house on his own. That... what was it called, planning a game?"

Feng Tao said, "It's a game design proposal, for an online game. A friend of mine is a big boss, and he's also a major shareholder in this shop. My nephew sold a proposal to him, and not only did he get him to cough up 200,000 yuan for it, but he's also going to invest millions to make the game. Hehe, make the game according to my nephew's ideas!"

The student couldn't help but ask, "A game like Legend of Mir?"

Feng Tao said, "Nope. They're making a free-to-play online game... There, the system's installed. Now I'll install the application software for you."

As noon approached, the computer was finally ready.

Feng Tao had the apprentice in his shop help the mother and son carry the computer downstairs and get a taxi.

He himself called his wife. "Chunhong, the stuff Guiliang wrote last night sold!"

"How much did it sell for?" Lin Chunhong was nursing their child.

"A full 100,000!"

Feng Tao, of course, had to be honest with his wife. His voice was trembling with excitement. "So awesome. Brother Gang actually bought it. I thought it was just waste paper."

Lin Chunhong was incredulous. "Are you kidding me?"

"Why would I lie to you?" Feng Tao said. "Guiliang is definitely going to make big money in the future. That kid has been super smart since he was little."

Lin Chunhong was confused. "Just a few pages of paper. President Tao didn't even need to buy it, he could have just memorized it."

"You don't get it." Feng Tao didn't understand it either, but that didn't stop him from acting like he did in front of his wife.

Lin Chunhong advised, "You should invite Guiliang over more often. We don't usually see that side of the family."

Feng Tao said, "You don't get it. I'm the closest relative to his family, even closer than his own second uncle. When his dad was little, he'd come stay at our house every chance he got, even if it meant walking for half a day."

The couple chatted for a while before the apprentice returned to the shop.

The apprentice was also very curious about it and asked in an envious tone, "Master, that Brother Chen from yesterday, did he really make 200,000 yuan just from writing something?"

"Why would I lie to you?" Feng Tao told the story with embellishments.

At noon, the apprentice took his boxed lunch and went to brag at the shop next door that sold Subor gaming consoles.

"Did you know? My master's nephew wrote something and sold it for 500,000 yuan!"

"You're full of shit."

"I swear I'm not lying. The guy's making an online game. He wrote a game design that's totally badass. He's still in high school, he's amazing with computers, and he even taught himself programming like a hacker."

"What's a hacker?"

"..."

In just half a day, the rumor had spread throughout the entire floor of shops: a student from County No. 2 High School named Chen Guiliang had made a game in his spare time and sold it to a big company for a whopping one million plus yuan!

"Who do I ask for the remaining 900,000?"
